newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian edible oil prices firm on low imports.
newsitem.headline: Indian edible oil prices firm on low imports.

text.p: Indian domestic edible oil prices have risen over the past week on reduced stocks and slow import arrivals, industry officials said on Wednesday.
"Edible oil prices have regained lost ground due to slow arrivals of imports," Navinbhai Shah, president of Bombay Oilseeds and Oil Exchange Ltd, told Reuters.
Traders said groundnut oil was quoted at 34,700 rupees per tonne against around 33,500 last week. Palm olein oil was quoted at 28,000 against 27,600.
Industry officials said traders were trying to buy and store large amounts of edible oil ahead of a possible nationwide strike by truck operators from April 1.
"Traders are trying to replenish stocks, fearing a strike by truck operators," Shah said.
Indian truck owners have threatened to stage a nationwide strike from April 1 in protest against a five percent service tax on road transport.
The tax was proposed by Finance Minister P. Chidambaram in the federal budget for the 1997/98 fiscal year beginning on April 1. A vote on the tax is expected in late April.
"Palm olein stocks have (become) depleted without imports but sunflower oil is regularly coming from the United States and Argentina," said one trader.
Industry officials said importers preferred sunflower oil because Malaysian palm olein prices were high.
They said they expected sunflower oil imports in the 1996/97 season (November-October) to rise to 450,000 tonnes from 120,000 in 1995/96.
"The domestic summer crop arrivals have started but they had slowed down during the last few days due to Holi," Shah said, referring to a Hindu festival to celebrate spring.

The Central Organisation of Oil Industry and Trade has forecast the summer oilseeds crop at 9.35 million tonnes, down from 9.55 million in the previous year. However, the Agriculture Ministry projects the summer crop at 9.7 million tonnes.
